targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: Governance 2026-06-15 (user-adjudicated, failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-672-series): reclassified weakens->non_contributory. V3-EXQ-672b fixed the 672a baseline-collapse instrumentation bug (now goal_success_rate_ARM_0=0.26, C6 PASS) and the completion gate fires (C3 PASS, 40.6% filtered, non_degenerate per check_degeneracy). But C1 (harm) and C2 (completion) FAIL because the gate ranks on a non-discriminative completion score: mean_candidate_score_spread_ARM_1=0.009 and mean_completion_signal is pinned ~0.3439 across both arms, so the dropped 40% are indistinguishable from the kept candidates (harm even rises slightly, ARM_1 0.343 > ARM_0 0.311, consistent with random removal). This is the monostrategy candidate-pool collapse (cf. ARC-065 GAP-A cand_world_pairwise_dist=0; V3-EXQ-543e/614e), surfaced on the hippocampal._score_trajectory channel. The run yields rich substrate information but no interpretable signal about whether MECH-057b's mechanism is correct -> non_contributory, not weakens. Note: MECH-057b had zero genuine prior evidence; this reclass returns it to zero (no illusory conflict resolution). Secondary: MECH-057b's claimed mechanism (HippocampalModule promotion policy) is unbuilt; 672b tests a harness quantile proxy. pending_retest_after_substrate gated on candidate-pool completion-score discriminability (ARC-065 GAP-A track).

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: 672b shows the MECH-057b completion gate ranks on hippocampal._score_trajectory, whose cross-candidate spread is ~0.009 (completion_signal flat ~0.3439 across arms) under the monostrategy candidate pool ARC-065 GAP-A targets. The completion-score channel is downstream of cand_world_pairwise_dist; once GAP-A route-range/SD-056 lands divergent per-candidate world predictions on a trained substrate, re-check that mean_candidate_score_spread rises before re-scoring the MECH-057b gate.

learning_extracted: MECH-057b's completion gate ranks on hippocampal._score_trajectory; under monostrategy candidate-pool collapse that score has ~0.009 cross-candidate spread, so the gate filters indistinguishable candidates and cannot help -- a substrate-ceiling, not a falsification.

The 672 series is progressive instrumentation-peeling (672 mis-scaled absolute threshold -> 672a resource_collected readout bug + baseline collapse -> 672b genuine substrate finding), converging on one structural property at 672b, not three independent bugs.
The flat-completion-score channel is the same candidate-pool collapse documented for z_world (ARC-065 GAP-A cand_world_pairwise_dist=0; 543e/614e); any per-candidate ranking gate inherits it.

MECH-057b's actual mechanism (HippocampalModule promotion policy) remains unbuilt; the experiment tests a harness quantile proxy -- a retest needs both a discriminable pool and, ultimately, the real promotion-policy path.
A future MECH-057b retest must carry a mean_candidate_score_spread non-vacuity precondition before scoring C1/C2 (the explicit guard against re-running the same vacuous contrast).

Same structural collapse as ARC-065 GAP-A (cand_world_pairwise_dist=0).
